name: Arona
lede: Arona is a dark, desaturated blue-grey, the kind of color a dictionary files under neutrals even though the color graph places it firmly among the slate blues.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this color to 1928; the library's own record disagrees with itself by one swatch letter, giving plate 39 J 6 in one field and 39 I 6 in another, a minor inconsistency rather than a real dispute [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes it as a dark bluish gray [1]. The nearest color-graph neighbor is [[dark-payne-s-grey]], 2.6 units away, with [[bruges]] close behind at 3.3, and [[dark-blue-slate]] and [[dark-blue-slate]] almost as close [2].

Munsell gives 9.0B 3.4/2.6, low in both lightness and chroma [1]. The hex #3E5563 is a screen approximation of the dictionary plate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey-blue in 274 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.15 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is a 1270 Italian panel, *The Mourning Saint John the Evangelist*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Lorenzo Lotto, Niels Larsen Stevns, Paul Signac, Jean Ranc and Vicente López Portaña all use it well above their peers' average rate [3]. Strong individual matches include Félix Ziem's *Venice from the Riva looking toward the Piazzale San Marco* (1885) and Henry Ottmann's *The Luxembourg Station in Brussels* (1903) [3]. The 1930s show the sharpest decade-level concentration, over seven times the archive's average [3]. These counts are computed matches, not pigment identifications [3].
